title: Titan WACC Build and Perpetuity Valuation Sensitivity
scenario: You're a junior analyst on the Mumbai equity desk, freshly handed a Titan valuation model. Your senior has locked in the assumptions — risk-free rate, beta, ERP, debt, tax rate — but left the WACC calculation and terminal value blank. She's also asked you to flag whether Titan's WACC should be classified as 'Low' or 'Medium' risk for portfolio review. Complete the WACC build-up and test how it drives terminal value.
instructions: Build Titan's cost of equity using CAPM, post-tax cost of debt, and blended WACC. Then compute perpetuity terminal value and risk-bucket the WACC. Use only cell formulas; all answers go in column B of the Answers sheet, referencing the Data sheet.
learning_objective: Compute Titan's WACC from first principles using CAPM inputs, derive the tax shield on debt, weight equity and debt correctly, and quantify how WACC drives terminal enterprise value under perpetual growth.
hints: Cost of Equity uses the formula Rf + Beta × ERP — look for these three numbers in row 3, 4, 5 of the Data sheet.
Post-tax cost of debt is the pre-tax rate multiplied by (1 minus tax rate). The tax shield cuts the interest cost by the marginal tax percentage.
WACC formula is (E/V)×Ke + (D/V)×Kd_after_tax, where E is equity market value (B9), D is debt (B8), and V is their sum. Use the Answers sheet cell refs for Ke and Kd_after_tax, sheet-qualified.

A2.value: Q1: Titan's Cost of Equity (Ke) using CAPM — Rf + Beta × ERP. Report as a percentage (e.g. 13.275).

A3.value: Q2: Post-tax Cost of Debt (Kd) = Pre-tax Kd × (1 − Tax Rate ÷ 100). Report as percentage.

A4.value: Q3: Titan's WACC = (E÷(E+D))×Ke + (D÷(E+D))×Kd_after_tax. Report as percentage.

A5.value: Q4: Recomputed Ke with Beta = 1.20 instead of 0.95. Report as percentage.

A6.value: Q5: Terminal Value using perpetuity: FCFF_FY26 × (1+g) ÷ (WACC−g), in ₹ Cr. Report as number.

A7.value: Q6: WACC Risk Bucket — if WACC < 10%, return 'Low'; if < 14%, return 'Medium'; else 'High'.
